summary: Assign a position within each ordered group.
syntax: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY group_column ORDER BY sort_column)
documentation: ROW_NUMBER numbers rows from one within each window partition. Its window ORDER BY controls numbering; a separate outer ORDER BY controls display. Add a unique tie-breaker for stable positions when primary sort values tie.
inputs: Window partition expressions and ordering expressions.
returns: A sequential integer for every row in its partition.
caution: ROW_NUMBER gives tied rows different numbers. RANK has different tie behavior; an unspecified tie order is not deterministic.
scenarios: Rank bookings within each service route.
Number purchases within each customer history.
Label queue positions for each branch office.
title: Number branch appointments
problem: From appointments(id INTEGER, branch TEXT, slot INTEGER), return id, branch and a column position. Number each branch starting at 1 by slot ascending, breaking ties by id ascending. Display rows ordered by branch, slot, id. All fields are non-NULL and id is unique.
goal: Use ROW_NUMBER() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Partition by branch, order the window by slot then id, and separately order the final rows.
